Our Story

Built on Experience. Trusted for Generations.

Long before Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics had a name, a building, or a sign on Hamilton Road, there was a young prosthetist and orthotist named James "Jim" Cheng who believed deeply in the difference his work could make in someone's life.

Jim began his career in the 1970s, bringing together a background in engineering, biomechanics and patient care. His education took him from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and the Hong Kong Government Physiotherapy School to further studies in prosthetics and orthotics at New York University. His career eventually brought him to Canada — first Toronto in 1972, then Winnipeg in 1975, and finally London in 1976.

From the beginning, Jim understood that his work was never simply about building a prosthesis or an orthosis. There was always a person on the other side of it. A person learning to walk again. A parent hoping their child could keep up with friends. Someone trying to return to work, drive a car, play a sport, or simply move through their day with less pain and greater independence. Those were the problems Jim dedicated his career to solving.

In 1988, after years of developing his craft, Jim opened Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics at 450 Hamilton Road in London, Ontario. His approach was simple: listen carefully, take the time to understand the person, build with care, and never stop working toward a better outcome. Patient by patient, family by family, that small independent practice grew — not because Hamilton became the biggest clinic, but because people trusted it. They came back when their needs changed. They brought their children. Physicians and rehabilitation professionals sent their patients. And over the years, many of the people who first walked through our doors as strangers became familiar faces we would have the privilege of caring for again and again. That trust became the foundation of Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics.

A Daughter Follows in Her Father's Footsteps

While Jim was building the practice, his daughter Shirley was growing up around it. She saw the finished prostheses and braces, but she also saw everything patients rarely see — the hours spent solving a difficult fitting problem, the adjustments made until something finally felt right, and the responsibility her father felt toward the people who trusted him with their care. Eventually, Shirley chose to follow the same path. She became a Canadian Certified Prosthetist and Orthotist, carrying forward the profession and the practice her father had devoted his life to building.

But following in Jim's footsteps never meant standing still.

Under Shirley's clinical leadership, Hamilton has embraced a new generation of prosthetic and orthotic care — from complex lower limb prosthetics and pediatric care to advanced myoelectric and bionic upper extremity systems and modern prosthetic technologies that would have been difficult to imagine when Jim first entered the profession. And yet, through all that change, something remarkably simple has remained the same. The person comes first.

Technology matters. Experience matters. Craftsmanship matters. But the most advanced device in the world means very little if it doesn't help someone live the life that matters to them. That lesson has been passed from father to daughter and continues to guide our team today.

Nearly Four Decades Later

Today, Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics remains at the same London location where Jim opened the doors in 1988 — still independent, still family owned, and now one of Southwestern Ontario's most trusted names in prosthetic and orthotic care.

Over the years, we have watched children grow up. We have seen people take their first steps after an amputation and later watched them return to work, family, hobbies and the lives they feared they might have lost. We have stood beside patients through setbacks, successes, new devices and changing needs. And sometimes, years later, we have had the extraordinary privilege of caring for another generation of the same family.

Those relationships are the history of Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics. Not the building. Not the technology. Not the devices we've made. The people.

Jim built the foundation. Shirley is carrying it forward. And every patient and family who has placed their trust in Hamilton has become part of the story. Nearly four decades after our doors first opened, our promise remains the same one Jim began with: Listen to the person. Care about the outcome. Build something that helps them move forward.

Because at Hamilton Prosthetics & Orthotics, we have never believed we are simply making prostheses and orthoses. We are helping people get back to the lives and the people they love.

Family owned. Independent. Trusted throughout Southwestern Ontario since 1988.

Our Approach to Care

01

Listen First

We take the time to understand each person — their needs, goals, challenges, and what they want to get back to doing.

02

Find the Right Solution

No two people are the same. We recommend the technology and design that best support each patient's lifestyle, abilities, and goals — not simply the most advanced option available.

03

Fit Matters

A successful device starts with comfort, function, and attention to detail. Our clinical and technical teams work closely together throughout the fitting and fabrication process.

04

Here for the Long Term

Our care doesn't end when a device is delivered. We continue to provide adjustments, maintenance, and ongoing support as our patients' needs change over time.
